doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Antagonism toward Lionel Hampton over treatment of sidemen
summary: Wilder says Hampton's band was hard to work in, citing how bassist Vernon Alley was dropped with only a ticket home when he fell ill in Texas.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: It wasn’t the easiest gig in the world, from what I understand.

It wasn’t, no it wasn’t. There were many times when it wasn’t. And the funny thing of it is that my antagonism towards Lionel didn’t come from anything he did to me personally, it was things that they did to other people that you were witness to you know. For instance the bass player, Vernon Alley, a very fine bass player, he became ill. We were someplace in Texas. And the doctor said he had the flu or something and he has to stay in bed for at least a week. And so it was like okay, they gave him the money that he had earned, we had played like maybe four days of that week, so they gave him salary for the four days and a ticket back — nothing extra — and a ticket back to California, a one way ticket, so he could go back home after he recuperated, and he just hired another bass player. He comes back, okay, you’re sick, goodbye. And things like that. It used to really get to me. I thought it was so mean and that’s one of the milder things.
